verses.original: מַה־ יָּפ֧וּ פְעָמַ֛יִךְ בַּנְּעָלִ֖ים בַּת־ נָדִ֑יב חַמּוּקֵ֣י יְרֵכַ֔יִךְ כְּמ֣וֹ חֲלָאִ֔ים מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְדֵ֥י אָמָּֽן׃
verses.transliteration: mah- yā·p̄ū p̄ə·‘ā·ma·yiḵ ban·nə·‘ā·lîm baṯ- nā·ḏîḇ ḥam·mū·qê yə·rê·ḵa·yiḵ kə·mōw ḥă·lā·’îm ma·‘ă·śêh yə·ḏê ’ām·mān
verses.literal: How beautiful are your sandaled feet O daughter of the prince The curves of your thighs are like jewels the handiwork . . . of a master
verses.literalPt: QUÃO formosos são os teus pés nos sapatos, ó filha do príncipe! Os contornos de tuas coxas são como jóias, trabalhadas por mãos de artista.

verses.original: שָׁרְרֵךְ֙ אַגַּ֣ן הַסַּ֔הַר אַל־ יֶחְסַ֖ר הַמָּ֑זֶג בִּטְנֵךְ֙ עֲרֵמַ֣ת חִטִּ֔ים סוּגָ֖ה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים׃
verses.transliteration: šā·rə·rêḵ ’ag·gan has·sa·har ’al- yeḥ·sar ham·mā·zeḡ biṭ·nêḵ ‘ă·rê·maṯ ḥiṭ·ṭîm sū·ḡāh baš·šō·wō·šan·nîm
verses.literal: Your navel is a rounded goblet it never lacks blended wine Your waist is a mound of wheat encircled by the lilies
verses.literalPt: O teu umbigo como uma taça redonda, a que não falta bebida; o teu ventre como montão de trigo, cercado de lírios.

verses.original: שְׁנֵ֥י שָׁדַ֛יִךְ כִּשְׁנֵ֥י עֳפָרִ֖ים תָּאֳמֵ֥י צְבִיָּֽה׃
verses.literal: Your breasts . . . are like two fawns twins of a gazelle
verses.literalPt: Os teus dois seios como dois filhos gêmeos de gazela.

verses.original: צַוָּארֵ֖ךְ כְּמִגְדַּ֣ל הַשֵּׁ֑ן עֵינַ֜יִךְ בְּרֵכ֣וֹת בְּחֶשְׁבּ֗וֹן עַל־ שַׁ֙עַר֙ בַּת־ רַבִּ֔ים אַפֵּךְ֙ כְּמִגְדַּ֣ל הַלְּבָנ֔וֹן צוֹפֶ֖ה פְּנֵ֥י דַמָּֽשֶׂק׃
verses.transliteration: ṣaw·wā·rêḵ kə·miḡ·dal haš·šên ‘ê·na·yiḵ bə·rê·ḵō·wṯ bə·ḥeš·bō·wn ‘al- ša·‘ar baṯ- rab·bîm ’ap·pêḵ kə·miḡ·dal hal·lə·ḇā·nō·wn ṣō·w·p̄eh pə·nê ḏam·mā·śeq
verses.literal: Your neck is like a tower made of ivory your eyes are like the pools of Heshbon by the gate of Bath-rabbim your nose is like the tower of Lebanon facing toward . . . Damascus
verses.literalPt: O teu pescoço como a torre de marfim; os teus olhos como as piscinas de Hesbom, junto à porta de Bate-Rabim; o teu nariz como torre do Líbano, que olha para Damasco.

verses.original: רֹאשֵׁ֤ךְ עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ כַּכַּרְמֶ֔ל וְדַלַּ֥ת רֹאשֵׁ֖ךְ כָּאַרְגָּמָ֑ן מֶ֖לֶךְ אָס֥וּר בָּרְהָטִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: rō·šêḵ ‘ā·la·yiḵ kak·kar·mel wə·ḏal·laṯ rō·šêḵ kā·’ar·gā·mān me·leḵ ’ā·sūr bā·rə·hā·ṭîm
verses.literal: Your head crowns you like Mount Carmel the hair of your head like purple threads the king is captured in your tresses
verses.literalPt: A tua cabeça sobre ti é como o monte Carmelo, e os cabelos da tua cabeça como a púrpura; o rei está preso nas galerias.

verses.original: מַה־ יָּפִית֙ וּמַה־ נָּעַ֔מְתְּ אַהֲבָ֖ה בַּתַּֽעֲנוּגִֽים׃
verses.literal: How fair and pleasant you are O love with your delights
verses.literalPt: Quão formosa, e quão aprazível és, ó amor em delícias!

verses.original: זֹ֤את קֽוֹמָתֵךְ֙ דָּֽמְתָ֣ה לְתָמָ֔ר וְשָׁדַ֖יִךְ לְאַשְׁכֹּלֽוֹת׃
verses.transliteration: zōṯ qō·w·mā·ṯêḵ dā·mə·ṯāh lə·ṯā·mār wə·šā·ḏa·yiḵ lə·’aš·kō·lō·wṯ
verses.literal: Your stature is like a palm tree your breasts are clusters of fruit
verses.literalPt: A tua estatura é semelhante à palmeira; e os teus seios são semelhantes aos cachos de uvas.

verses.original: אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ אֶעֱלֶ֣ה בְתָמָ֔ר אֹֽחֲזָ֖ה בְּסַנְסִנָּ֑יו וְיִֽהְיוּ־ נָ֤א שָׁדַ֙יִךְ֙ כְּאֶשְׁכְּל֣וֹת הַגֶּ֔פֶן וְרֵ֥יחַ אַפֵּ֖ךְ כַּתַּפּוּחִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: ’ā·mar·tî ’e·‘ĕ·leh ḇə·ṯā·mār ’ō·ḥă·zāh bə·san·sin·nāw wə·yih·yū- nā šā·ḏa·yiḵ kə·’eš·kə·lō·wṯ hag·ge·p̄en wə·rê·aḥ ’ap·pêḵ kat·tap·pū·ḥîm
verses.literal: I said I will climb the palm tree I will take hold of its fruit May your breasts be . . . like clusters of the vine the fragrance of your breath like apples
verses.literalPt: Dizia eu: Subirei à palmeira, pegarei em seus ramos; e então os teus seios serão como os cachos na vide, e o cheiro da tua respiração como o das maçãs.

verses.original: וְחִכֵּ֕ךְ כְּיֵ֥ין הַטּ֛וֹב הוֹלֵ֥ךְ לְדוֹדִ֖י לְמֵישָׁרִ֑ים דּוֹבֵ֖ב שִׂפְתֵ֥י יְשֵׁנִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: wə·ḥik·kêḵ kə·yên haṭ·ṭō·wḇ hō·w·lêḵ lə·ḏō·w·ḏî lə·mê·šā·rîm dō·w·ḇêḇ śip̄·ṯê yə·šê·nîm
verses.literal: and your mouth like the finest wine May it flow smoothly to my beloved gliding gently over lips and teeth
verses.literalPt: E a tua boca como o bom vinho para o meu amado, que se bebe suavemente, e faz com que falem os lábios dos que dormem.

verses.literal: I belong to my beloved and his desire is for me
verses.literalPt: Eu sou do meu amado, e ele me tem afeição.

verses.original: לְכָ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ נֵצֵ֣א הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה נָלִ֖ינָה בַּכְּפָרִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: lə·ḵāh ḏō·w·ḏî nê·ṣê haś·śā·ḏeh nā·lî·nāh bak·kə·p̄ā·rîm
verses.literal: Come my beloved let us go to the countryside let us spend the night among the wildflowers
verses.literalPt: Vem, ó amado meu, saiamos ao campo, passemos as noites nas aldeias.

verses.original: נַשְׁכִּ֙ימָה֙ לַכְּרָמִ֔ים נִרְאֶ֞ה אִם פָּֽרְחָ֤ה הַגֶּ֙פֶן֙ פִּתַּ֣ח הַסְּמָדַ֔ר הֵנֵ֖צוּ הָרִמּוֹנִ֑ים שָׁ֛ם אֶתֵּ֥ן אֶת־ דֹּדַ֖י לָֽךְ׃
verses.transliteration: naš·kî·māh lak·kə·rā·mîm nir·’eh ’im pā·rə·ḥāh hag·ge·p̄en pit·taḥ has·sə·mā·ḏar hê·nê·ṣū hā·rim·mō·w·nîm šām ’et·tên ’eṯ- dō·ḏay lāḵ
verses.literal: Let us go early to the vineyards to see if the vine has budded if the blossom . . . has opened if the pomegranates are in bloom there I will give you my love
verses.literalPt: Levantemo-nos de manhã para ir às vinhas, vejamos se florescem as vides, se já aparecem as tenras uvas, se já brotam as romãzeiras; ali te darei os meus amores.

verses.original: הַֽדּוּדָאִ֣ים נָֽתְנוּ־ רֵ֗יחַ וְעַל־ פְּתָחֵ֙ינוּ֙ כָּל־ מְגָדִ֔ים חֲדָשִׁ֖ים גַּם־ יְשָׁנִ֑ים דּוֹדִ֖י צָפַ֥נְתִּי לָֽךְ׃
verses.transliteration: had·dū·ḏā·’îm nā·ṯə·nū- rê·aḥ wə·‘al- pə·ṯā·ḥê·nū kāl- mə·ḡā·ḏîm ḥă·ḏā·šîm gam- yə·šā·nîm dō·w·ḏî ṣā·p̄an·tî lāḵ
verses.literal: The mandrakes send forth a fragrance and at our door is every delicacy new as well as old that I have treasured up for you my beloved
verses.literalPt: As mandrágoras exalam o seu perfume, e às nossas portas há todo o gênero de excelentes frutos, novos e velhos; ó amado meu, eu os guardei para ti.
